title: Conviction and Doubt
setting: A stone cell with three stools and a door that is not locked. Each of them has been condemned by a court that followed its own procedures correctly. Each of them could have escaped and did not.
stakes: Whether certainty is a virtue or the failure that gets people killed - and whether refusing to run was courage or vanity.

roles_in_scene.joan-of-arc: Nineteen, condemned for heresy, and entirely certain about the voices
roles_in_scene.socrates: Seventy, condemned for impiety, and certain of nothing except the value of asking
roles_in_scene.marcus-aurelius: Not condemned by anyone, which is the thing the other two will not let him forget

opening_line: Three people who could have walked out. One door, and it is not locked.
